- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (especially >70), overshooting by 2–5% in next 3–5 days; apply dampening factor to peak forecasts.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to anticipate rebound; add 1–2% upward adjustment in forecast horizon.  
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true price by 1–3 days; adjust for lag by adding 0.5–1.5% to forecast for early days of the 30d window.  
- If sentiment history shows volatility spikes (e.g., 0.8 → 1.0 → 0.2), model tends to misjudge direction; use sentiment transition as signal to adjust slope of forecast curve.
